fields.platform: Microsoft Bob 1995 Win16 NE binaries → portable C recompilation hosted by the project's cross-platform runtime; project README targets Windows, macOS, and Linux.
fields.status: Bring-up; the maintainer reports that the six Bob and Jet/Access Basic modules lift to link-clean C, Bob's real startup and MFC window creation execute, and Jet opens the original databases. The current blocker is a host longjmp/stack fault before the first rendered frame; no GUI frame or usable application release is claimed.
fields.summary: Static recompilation of the original Win16 Bob house application, its engine, blitter, and load-bearing Jet/Access Basic modules into C. The host/runtime reconstructs Win16, Jet, and WinG behavior; the project has reached real application initialization and database opens but has not yet drawn the Bob house. Original binaries, data, and lifted C are user-generated and are not distributed.
fields.source_available: Public MIT-licensed tooling, runtime, hand-written code, and analysis metadata. Original Bob binaries/data and generated lifted C are not included and are not covered by the repository MIT license; users must provide their own disc files.

sources.label: Microsoft Bob maintainer README: platform, six-module lift, current startup/database milestones, blocker, build requirements, and license boundary
Microsoft Bob repository license: MIT applies to repository-owned code, not original binaries or generated lifted C

updates.evidence_note: The existing row already identified Bob as a Win16 recompilation, but its platform and status understated the newly documented cross-platform target and current bring-up. This patch preserves the distinction between successful initialization/database work and a still-unrendered application.
